use /lib
use /ui
from /ui/theme import ThemeScope
from /ui/components/scrollbar import ScrollbarScope

export ui-component TaskTableScope:
    concept: {TaskTableConcept}

concept TaskTableConcept:
    pitch:
        The output of one run of the harness, as a table of everything it did,
        filling in as it does it.

    shape: {TaskTableShape}

shape TaskTableShape:
    description:
        A table with Type, Output, and Status columns, with one row per thing
        the harness did, in order: each piece of reply text, each tool call, and
        any error. It is the same table wherever a run's output is shown, a
        task, a question, a previous task or answer, the palette's search for a
        file, or a run in one of the application's own panels, and each use
        says where it sits.

    types:
        Type is a coloured badge with an icon. Reply text is "Reply" and errors
        are "Error". Tool calls are "Files" for Read, Glob, Grep, LS, and
        NotebookRead; "Edit" for Edit, MultiEdit, Write, and NotebookEdit;
        "Command" for Bash, BashOutput, KillShell, and KillBash; "Web" for
        WebFetch and WebSearch; "Agent" for Task and Agent; and "Tool" for
        anything else.

    status:
        A tool call's status is "running", "done", or "failed", and a call still
        running when the run ends takes the state the run ended in.

    replies:
        Reply text is rendered as markdown, with no border around it. What
        subagents do is left out. If nothing streamed but the harness reports a
        final result, that result is shown as the reply. A finished run with
        nothing to show reads "No output."

    toolCalls:
        A tool call's Output cell shows its most telling argument. For Files,
        Edit, Command, Web, and Agent calls the tool's name is left out, since
        the badge already says what it is; any other tool's name comes first.

        Any path inside the project directory is shown relative to it, and the
        project directory itself reads `.`.

        A command is shown whole, as a syntax-highlighted bash block, and a long
        one is split across lines at `&&`, `||`, `|`, and `;`, one command per
        line with the chained ones indented. It never splits inside quotes,
        command substitutions, brackets, comments, or heredocs. Other arguments
        are shown on a single line.

    streaming:
        While the run is under way, the table ends in a waiting row for
        whatever the harness does next. Until a row has something meaningful to
        show, its Type cell is a skeleton and its Output cell shows the last
        three lines of the harness's raw JSON output: muted, monospace, JSON
        syntax-highlighted, and always three lines tall so the row doesn't jump.
        Before any output has arrived it reads "Waiting for the harness…". As
        soon as a row's type is known, its badge is real, and as soon as its
        text or argument arrives, that is shown. While the input of a Files,
        Edit, Command, Web, or Agent call is still arriving, its Output cell
        shows only a skeleton.

        A skeleton stands in for a running row only while there is nothing
        meaningful to show for it. As soon as there is, no skeleton is shown for
        it at all.

    header:
        The header row, reading Type, Output, and Status, has the bevel of the
        @{ThemeScope}, lifting it slightly off the rows beneath.

    scrolling:
        The rows scroll beneath the table's header, which stays at the top,
        with a @{ScrollbarScope}, usually with its lock to the bottom. Locked,
        the table follows the run's latest output. Unlocked, it still follows
        new output while it is already scrolled to the bottom, and stays put
        once scrolled away from it. Each use says whether its table has the
        lock, and whether it starts on.

        However long the output grows, drawing it costs no more than drawing
        the rows in view, so scrolling, animations, and new output stay smooth.
        While the end of the table is scrolled out of view, raw output that
        would only change the waiting row redraws nothing.

    collapsedSteps:
        A use can say its table collapses the steps leading up to the answer,
        once the run is finished. The steps are every row up to and including
        the harness's last tool call; the answer is the rows after it. In their
        place, the table's first row reads "Show 1 step" or "Show N steps",
        muted, beside a right chevron, with the answer beneath it. A single
        click on that row expands the steps in place, above the answer, and the
        row then reads "Hide 1 step" or "Hide N steps" beside a down chevron;
        clicking it again collapses them. Each table is expanded or collapsed on
        its own.

        A run with no tool calls, or with nothing after its last one, has
        nothing to collapse and shows whole. A run still under way shows its
        latest step as usual.

    legibility:
        The output from a realtime agent should be readable and meaningful.
        Make sure the font size is large enough, and that the colours are
        legible in both light and dark mode.

export ui-component HistoryListScope:
    concept: {HistoryListConcept}

concept HistoryListConcept:
    pitch:
        A way back to everything sent before of one kind, such as previous tasks
        or previous answers: a small row that expands into a list of every one
        of them.

    shape: {HistoryListShape}

shape HistoryListShape:
    description:
        The same row and list, looking and behaving the same, wherever something
        sent before can be looked back on. Each use names what it lists, what
        the row counts, and what the row reads while expanded.

    row:
        A small row, always shown where it is used, with the tab bar's
        background colour. It reads "No …", "1 …", or "N …" followed by what it
        counts, beside a chevron, and does nothing until there is anything to
        list. Clicking it expands the list, and the row then reads what it says
        to go back; clicking it again closes the list.

    list:
        A scrollable accordion of every item, oldest first, with a
        @{ScrollbarScope}. Each time it is expanded, it opens scrolled to the
        bottom, with the most recent items in view, however it was scrolled when
        last closed, the first time as much as any other, and whether it takes
        the place of the latest task or slides up as a drawer. Each is headed by
        its status and the first line of its prompt, and opens onto the compiled
        prompt it was sent as and its @{TaskTableScope}. One item is open at a
        time. A use can say its tables collapse the steps leading up to the
        result, as previous answers do; previous tasks show their tables whole.

        An open item is exactly as wide as the list, however long the lines
        in its prompt or table, which wrap rather than running past the
        list's edge, and exactly as tall as what it shows: it ends a small
        margin below its table, like the margin above its prompt, with no
        empty space beneath it before the next item or the end of the list.
        waiting row for whatever the harness does next. Tasks never collapse
        their steps, since their whole chain is of interest.

    links:
        Links in the compiled prompt and in reply text are clickable. A link to
        a file opens it, as the @{OpenFileScope} says, and a web link opens in
        the browser. The file path on a Read, Edit, Write, or MultiEdit row is
        shown as a link and opens that file the same way.

    backgrounds:
        The header for the latest task is coloured like the tab the task was
        sent from, the colour of its mode, of the @{PromptModesScope}, as the
        @{ChatInputScope} body shows for that tab. A task from the history that
        doesn't say which tab it was sent from keeps the tab bar's colour. The
        queue along the bottom and the previous tasks row along the top both
        have the same background colour as the tab bar.

    askDimming:
        While the @{AnswerDrawerScope} is open, it dims the message list beneath
        it.

    scrolling:
        The latest task's table scrolls with its lock to the bottom off to
        start with, until switched on.

        However long the list of previous tasks grows, drawing it costs no more
        than drawing the tasks in view, so scrolling, animations, and new output
        stay smooth.

    description:
        The same row and list, looking and behaving the same, wherever something
        sent before can be looked back on. Each use names what it lists, what
        the row counts, and what the row reads while expanded.

    row:
        A small row, always shown where it is used, with the tab bar's
        background colour. It reads "No …", "1 …", or "N …" followed by what it
        counts, beside a chevron, and does nothing until there is anything to
        list. Clicking it expands the list, and the row then reads what it says
        to go back; clicking it again closes the list.

    list:
        A scrollable accordion of every item, oldest first, with a
        @{ScrollbarScope}. Each time it is expanded, it opens scrolled to the
        bottom, with the most recent items in view, however it was scrolled when
        last closed, the first time as much as any other, and whether it takes
        the place of the latest task or slides up as a drawer. Each is headed by
        its status and the first line of its prompt, and opens onto the compiled
        prompt it was sent as and its @{TaskTableScope}. One item is open at a
        time. A use can say its tables collapse the steps leading up to the
        result, as previous answers do; previous tasks show their tables whole.

        An open item is exactly as wide as the list, however long the lines
        in its prompt or table, which wrap rather than running past the
        list's edge, and exactly as tall as what it shows: it ends a small
        margin below its table, like the margin above its prompt, with no
        empty space beneath it before the next item or the end of the list.
        waiting row for whatever the harness does next. Tasks never collapse
        their steps, since their whole chain is of interest.

    links:
        Links in the compiled prompt and in reply text are clickable. A link to
        a file opens it, as the @{OpenFileScope} says, and a web link opens in
        the browser. The file path on a Read, Edit, Write, or MultiEdit row is
        shown as a link and opens that file the same way.

    backgrounds:
        The header for the latest task is coloured like the tab the task was
        sent from, the colour of its mode, of the @{PromptModesScope}, as the
        @{ChatInputScope} body shows for that tab. A task from the history that
        doesn't say which tab it was sent from keeps the tab bar's colour. The
        queue along the bottom and the previous tasks row along the top both
        have the same background colour as the tab bar.

    askDimming:
        While the @{AnswerDrawerScope} is open, it dims the message list beneath
        it.

    scrolling:
        The latest task's table scrolls with its lock to the bottom off to
        start with, until switched on.

        However long the list of previous tasks grows, drawing it costs no more
        than drawing the tasks in view, so scrolling, animations, and new output
        stay smooth.

palette:
        Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on macOS) opens the @{PaletteScope} over the window, for
        fuzzy searching the project's files, the application's own commands, and
        the commands, skills, and agents of the @{HarnessCatalogScope}.

    header:
        ribbon: @{RibbonScope}

    body:
        sidebar: @{SidebarScope}

        openFile:
            A file opened, from the @{FileTreeScope} or anywhere else the
            @{OpenFileScope} says, shows in an @{EditorScope}, in a split beside
            the chat history: the file on the left taking 50%
            of the width, the chat history on the right taking the rest. The
            split can be resized by dragging its edge. Closing the file closes
            the split.

            When the split opens, it slides in from the sidebar, so it's clear
            where it came from: the file's side grows out of the sidebar's edge
            to its share of the width, the file sliding into view from behind
            that edge as it does, while the chat history gives way beside it.
            The slide is quick and settles without bouncing, and only then can
            the split be dragged. A file opened in place of one already showing
            doesn't slide, since the split is already open. The
            @{ChatInputScope} is never split: it stays along the bottom, across
            the full width of prompt mode.

            Closing the file plays the slide in reverse, back into the
            sidebar: the file's side shrinks from whatever width it was
            dragged to down to nothing at the sidebar's edge, the file sliding
            out of view behind that edge as it does, while the chat history
            grows back across the full width. It is as quick as the slide in,
            and settles without bouncing. Opening a file while one is still
            sliding out slides the new one in straight away.

        openDiff:
            A file's @{DiffViewScope}, opened from the @{FileTreeScope}, opens
            in an @{InsetPanelScope}. It leaves the split alone: any file open
            there stays open, unsaved changes and all. Opening another file's
            diff replaces the one in the panel, as does opening one while a new
            project is being set up. Opening the file from the diff closes the
            panel and opens the file, as the @{OpenFileScope} says.

        analyzeDivergence:
            The ribbon's Analyze Divergence command opens the @{DivergenceScope}
            as a @{MinimizablePanelScope}, to analyze, in place of whatever else
            is open there, or brings back one that was minimized.

This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

content.text:
Every place that shows a run's output now uses the same virtualized table: the latest task, the answer drawer, both history lists, the palette search, and the divergence, rescope and generate-skills panels. All tests pass (220, 1 ignored), dev and release builds have no warnings, and the piton checks and build pass. I haven't run the app itself, so none of this has been checked by eye or timed.

**One change from your plan.** I used `with_uniform_item_height`, but gpui throws those guesses away whenever the list's width changes. From then on it counts unseen rows as zero height, which is exactly what caused the jumping before. So the scrollbar doesn't read gpui's heights anymore:
- The list keeps its own height for every row (`src/measured_list.rs`). Rows in view are recorded as gpui draws them, and the rest are measured in the background, about 4ms of work per frame, until all are known.
- A row not yet measured counts as tall as it last was, or as the average of rows measured so far.
- The guesses are handed back to gpui in the same frame, so wheel scrolling doesn't slip into zero-height rows.
- After a width change, only the rows in view are laid out straight away.

**What else changed**
- **The table** (`src/task_table.rs`) owns its list and keeps its header above the rows as they scroll.
- **Rows:** `Reply` keeps its row list and a log of which rows changed as events arrive. Drawing a row is a direct lookup, and only new or changed rows are measured again.
- **History:** an open item's prompt, header, each table row and its end are rows of the history list itself, so a long open item costs only what's in view.
- **Cached output:**
  - The cleaned markdown is stored on each text part and compiled prompt.
  - The formatted command is stored on the tool call.
  - Each raw line's JSON highlighting is worked out once.
  - Markdown is prepared only for rows being drawn or measured.
- **Pane slide:** the editor now slides over the task view, which keeps its width until the slide settles. When closing, the task view is back at full width underneath from the start.
- **Markdown parse notices:** each table now tracks its own place in the list of finished parses. Before, the first view to read that list emptied it for everyone else.

**Tests**
- **New test:** a 1,500-row task, which checks:
  - a frame, including the one where the window narrows, draws under a quarter of the rows;
  - the rows in view stay put while the rest are measured;
  - once measured, the thumb holds still;
  - rows added below while you're scrolled up don't move the output.
- **Check on the new test:** with the per-frame budget made unlimited, so every row is measured in one frame, it fails.
- **Existing scrollbar-stability tests:** they now wait until every row is measured, then check as before.
- **Main window test:** it checks that the chat history keeps its width while the file slides in and out.
- **Other adjusted tests:** one counts answer rows after the drawer finishes opening, since rows below the view aren't drawn anymore. The history test checks the new end-of-item row.

**Behaviour you might notice**
- For a few frames after a big change the thumb can move a little as it settles: opening a long history item, switching to a long task, or resizing. After that it holds still.
- Dragging the thumb before a long table has finished measuring isn't covered by a test.
- When the file finishes sliding in, the task view narrows once.

I updated the spec for the task table, the history list and the main window's slide. `git status` also shows five `.suspense` history and ask files that I didn't create; I left them alone.

tool_input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='src/task_table.rs'
s=open(p).read()
def rep(old,new,count=1):
    global s
    assert s.count(old)==count, (s.count(old), old[:90])
    s=s.replace(old,new)
rep("use gpui_kit::component::{ActiveTheme as _, Icon, Sizable as _, h_flex, v_flex};","use gpui_kit::component::{ActiveTheme as _, Icon, Sizable as _, StyledExt as _, h_flex, v_flex};")
rep("Rc<JsonStyles>)>>>,","Arc<JsonStyles>)>>>,")
rep("let styles = Rc::new(json_highlights(line, theme));","let styles = Arc::new(json_highlights(line, theme));")
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='src/prompt_mode.rs'
s=open(p).read()
rep("""    self, Compiled as _, Layout as TableLayout, OutputRow, Reply, Steps, TableSync, TableView,
    TaskTable, ToolKind, relative_to_project, shown_markdown_view,""","""    self, KIND_WIDTH, Layout as TableLayout, OutputRow, Reply, STATUS_WIDTH, Steps, TableSync,
    TableView, TaskTable, ToolKind, relative_to_project, row_status, shown_markdown_view,""")
rep("use std::cell::Cell;","use std::cell::{Cell, RefCell};")
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='src/chat_input.rs'
s=open(p).read()
rep("crate::prompt_mode::markdown_view(","crate::task_table::markdown_view(")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
cargo build 2>&1 | grep -E "^error" -A12 | grep -v "^\s*|$" | head -80
cargo test prompt_mode::tests::an_answer 2>&1 | grep -E "panicked|test result" -A4 | cut -c1-300; cargo test prompt_mode::tests::tool_name 2>&1 | grep -E "panicked|test result" -A4 | cut -c1-300
